title: Complex systems are much easier to understand when you can interact with them instead of a diagram.
note: Owner saved it as a model for interactive 'how a complicated machine works' visuals and for how to plan future Shorts.

analysis.topic: Anatomy, a free open-source Claude Code skill that builds interactive machines (SVG, WebGL) to show how complicated things work; 'Hidden GitHub Gems' series, part of a series
analysis.format: talking head cut with screen demo of an interactive diagram
analysis.hook: Names the payoff in one sentence: 'This new GitHub repo can take almost any complicated machine and show you exactly how it works with an interactive visual.' Then a fast cut to the person and a bold on-screen word per beat.
structure: 0-5 s: the promise (any complicated machine, shown interactively) + who it is for
5-12 s: the pain it removes (hours of videos or confusing diagrams) and the example prompt: 'Show me how SpaceX's rocket engine works'
12-22 s: the demo: hover the model, the engine separates into 11 assemblies, an animated version
22-30 s: the twist: not AI images, real code (SVG, WebGL, 3D), so parts move and respond
30-38 s: uses (engines, how a computer processes information, software systems), export, free and open source, series tag
analysis.visual_style: creator on camera in a clean room with a studio microphone, alternating with a light-background screen demo of orange, black and green gears; large white captions, one or two words at a time; moody b-roll for the opening line
why_it_works: A concrete example subject everyone is curious about (a rocket engine) instead of an abstract tool pitch
Shows the result moving in the first seconds: 'interactive instead of a diagram' is understood without explanation
One idea, one escalation (11 assemblies, then animated, then 'not AI images, real code'), then an easy ask
Series framing ('Hidden GitHub Gems, part N') brings viewers back
analysis.reuse: Explain how a complex machine works by pulling it apart: an exploded, animated diagram where each assembly appears with its one job and a real number - the 'anatomy of a machine' Short.
adaptations: How a jet engine works, taken apart part by part
How a nuclear reactor makes electricity, taken apart part by part
How the Large Hadron Collider works, step by step through its parts
How a mechanical watch works: the escapement and the gear train, taken apart
How a submarine makes its own air and water, system by system
analysis.avoid: Do not copy the title, script, series tag or the creator's footage; do not make tutorials or tool demos (AI tools flop on this channel). Use the idea of an animated exploded diagram with our own subjects and facts.
